message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"11","text":"Therefore, since you truly are disciples of a prophet, lay aside the discord from which wrongdoing arises and eagerly undertake to do good. But if any of you doubts that what has been said will happen, let him admit it without shame, provided that he cares for his own soul, and he will be fully assured by the one who presides. But if he has believed rightly, let him confidently conduct his life as one fleeing a great fire of condemnation and entering God’s everlasting, good kingdom.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προφήτου ἀληθῶς ὄντες μαθηταί","chosen":"since you truly are disciples of a prophet","rationale":"Leaves the prophet unnamed and preserves the emphasis that the addressees truly are his disciples."},{"source_quote":"προθύμως τὸ εὖ ποιεῖν ἀναδέξασθε","chosen":"eagerly undertake to do good","rationale":"Renders ἀναδέξασθε as willingly taking up a responsibility rather than merely beginning an action."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ προεστῶτος πληροφορηθήσεται","chosen":"he will be fully assured by the one who presides","rationale":"Preserves the passive sense of receiving assurance and does not import a more specific ecclesiastical title."},{"source_quote":"θαρρῶν πολιτευέσθω","chosen":"let him confidently conduct his life","rationale":"Takes πολιτεύεσθαι as living or conducting oneself, with θαρρῶν supplying confidence."},{"source_quote":"εἰς ἀιδίαν ἀγαθὴν θεοῦ βασιλείαν εἰσερχόμενος","chosen":"entering God’s everlasting, good kingdom","rationale":"Preserves both adjectives applied to the kingdom and its attribution to God."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"12","text":"The deacons of the church, then, should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about discerningly and examining the actions of each person in the church to see who is about to sin, so that, when caught by the admonition of the one who presides, he perhaps may not go through with the sin at all. They should bring back those who desert their posts, so that those who gather do not fail to listen to the discourses, in order that they may be able, through the word of truth, to cleanse away the discouragements that from time to time fall upon the heart from both life’s misfortunes and evil associations. For whenever they have lain uncultivated for a long time, they become material for fire. They should also ascertain who are ill in the flesh and make them known to the multitude that is unaware, so that they may appear, and they should provide what is needed according to the judgment of the one who presides. Even if they do this secretly, without his knowledge, they do not sin. The deacons, then, should take thought for these and similar matters.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνετῶς ῥεμβόμενοι ἔστωσαν ὀφθαλμοί","chosen":"should be the bishop’s eyes, moving about discerningly","rationale":"Preserves both the image of the deacons as eyes and their discerning movement through the community."},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστου τῆς ἐκκλησίας πολυπραγμονοῦντες τὰς πράξεις","chosen":"examining the actions of each person in the church","rationale":"Renders the intensive scrutiny expressed by πολυπραγμονοῦντες without adding a judgment about the legitimacy of that scrutiny."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς λειποτάκτας ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν","chosen":"They should bring back those who desert their posts","rationale":"Retains the military image of λειποτάκτας while expressing ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν as restoring them to participation."},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","chosen":"For whenever they have lain uncultivated for a long time, they become material for fire","rationale":"Preserves the image of land lying uncultivated and the ensuing fire image while leaving the plural subject unstated."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα νοσοῦντας","chosen":"who are ill in the flesh","rationale":"Retains the explicit bodily qualification supplied by κατὰ σάρκα."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","chosen":"and make them known to the multitude that is unaware, so that they may appear","rationale":"Uses a deliberately provisional rendering that does not reduce ἐπιφαίνωνται to passive publicity; the possible subjects and precise action remain uncertain."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται","issue":"The precise force of προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν and the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται are uncertain. The physically ill may be made known and then appear or present themselves, but the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται could instead be members of the previously unaware multitude coming on the scene, perhaps to visit or assist the sick; that purpose is contextually possible but is not explicitly stated by the verb.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἂν χρόνῳ πολλῷ χερσεύσωσιν, πυρὸς ἔργον γίνονται","issue":"The antecedent of the plural verbs χερσεύσωσιν and γίνονται is not explicit. The referent may be the discouragements, the hearers, or people considered through the implied image of uncultivated ground. The translation retains an unresolved “they.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"13","text":"Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize, for the work concerns human souls. The instructor in the discourses must adapt himself to the many dispositions of those who are learning. The one who catechizes must therefore be widely learned, above reproach, highly experienced, and fearless, as you yourselves will find Clement—who is to catechize after me—to be. For it would take too long for me now to discuss the matter item by item. Nevertheless, if you are of one mind, you will be able to be carried into the harbor of rest, where there is the peaceful city of a great king.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ κατηχοῦντες πρῶτον κατηχήθέντες κατηχείτωσαν","chosen":"Those who catechize should first be catechized and then catechize","rationale":"Preserves the repeated κατηχέω word family and the required sequence of first receiving and then giving instruction."},{"source_quote":"ὅτι περὶ ψυχῆς ἀνθρώπων τὸ ἔργον","chosen":"for the work concerns human souls","rationale":"Expresses the compressed singular Greek phrase idiomatically without diminishing its concern for the souls of human beings."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς γὰρ τὰς πολλὰς τῶν μανθανόντων γνώμας συναρμόζεσθαι","chosen":"must adapt himself to the many dispositions of those who are learning","rationale":"Takes γνώμαι as the varied dispositions or outlooks of learners and συναρμόζεσθαι as adapting instruction accordingly."},{"source_quote":"πολὺ γὰρ ἐστὶν ἐμὲ νῦν τὸ κατ’ εἶδος λέγειν","chosen":"For it would take too long for me now to discuss the matter item by item","rationale":"Understands κατ’ εἶδος as detailed treatment according to each particular and πολὺ as indicating that such treatment would be extensive."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν τῆς ἀναπαύσεως ἐνεχθῆναι λιμένα","chosen":"to be carried into the harbor of rest","rationale":"Retains the passive nautical image that introduces the extended ship allegory of the following sections."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"14","text":"For the whole enterprise of the church resembles a large ship carrying through a fierce storm men who are from many places and who wish to inhabit one particular city belonging to a good kingdom. Let God, then, be the master of this ship for you, and let the helmsman be likened to the Messiah, the bow officer to the bishop, the sailors to the elders, the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons, the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize, the multitude of the brothers to the passengers, the deep sea to the world, and the contrary winds to the temptations. Let the persecutions, dangers, and afflictions of every kind be likened to the towering waves; the offshore winds of the torrents and the gusts to the discourses of deceivers and false prophets; the promontories and rough places to judges in positions of authority who threaten terrible things; and places between two seas and beast-infested places to those who are irrational and doubtful about the promises of the truth. Let the hypocrites be understood as likened to pirates. Nevertheless, regard sins alone as a mighty whirlpool, a Tartarean Charybdis, murderous collisions, and deadly breakups. Therefore, so that, sailing with a fair wind, you may be carried more safely into the harbor of the hoped-for city, pray so as to be heard; and prayers are heard through good deeds.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὅλον τὸ πρᾶγμα τῆς ἐκκλησίας","chosen":"the whole enterprise of the church","rationale":"Renders πρᾶγμα broadly as the church’s entire undertaking or organized affair."},{"source_quote":"ὁ μὲν κυβερνήτης χριστῷ","chosen":"the helmsman be likened to the Messiah","rationale":"Preserves the nautical office and renders independently titular χριστός as “Messiah.”"},{"source_quote":"ὁ πρωρεὺς ἐπισκόπῳ, οἱ ναῦται πρεσβυτέροις, οἱ τοίχαρχοι διακόνοις, οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοῖς κατηχοῦσιν","chosen":"the bow officer to the bishop, the sailors to the elders, the officers of the ship’s sides to the deacons, the ship’s recruiters to those who catechize","rationale":"Maintains the differentiated shipboard roles rather than flattening them into a generic crew."},{"source_quote":"τὰ δὲ ἀπόγεια τῶν χειμάρρων καὶ τὰ φυσήματα","chosen":"the offshore winds of the torrents and the gusts","rationale":"Represents ἀπόγεια as winds blowing away from land and preserves the supplied genitive τῶν χειμάρρων rather than replacing “torrents” with “storms.”"},{"source_quote":"ταρταρέαν χάρυβδιν","chosen":"a Tartarean Charybdis","rationale":"Retains both the underworld characterization and the named mythological maritime hazard."},{"source_quote":"ἐπηκόως εὔχεσθε· εὐχαὶ δὲ ἐπήκοοι γίνονται ταῖς εὐπραγίαις","chosen":"pray so as to be heard; and prayers are heard through good deeds","rationale":"Preserves the repeated language of being heard and the author’s stated connection between heard prayer and good conduct."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὰ δὲ ἀπόγεια τῶν χειμάρρων καὶ τὰ φυσήματα","issue":"The expression is semantically compressed. ἀπόγεια can denote winds blowing from land, while τῶν χειμάρρων ordinarily means “of the torrents” or “of the winter-swollen streams.” The precise relationship of those torrents to the offshore winds is unclear. The translation preserves the supplied genitive provisionally and does not treat χειμάρρων as a form of χειμών or substitute “storms.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"15","text":"The passengers, then, should keep steady, seated firmly in their own places, so that through disorder they do not cause rocking or a list to one side. The ship’s recruiters should give reminders of the rewards. The deacons should neglect none of the things entrusted to them. The elders, like sailors, should carefully prepare what is needed for each person. The bishop, like a bow officer keeping watch, should relay the words of the helmsman alone. The Messiah, as Savior and helmsman, should be loved, and he alone should be trusted concerning what he says. All of them should pray to God that they may sail with a fair wind. Those sailing should expect every affliction as they sail past a great and turbulent deep—the world—at one time becoming discouraged, persecuted, scattered, hungry, thirsty, naked, and distressed, and again at another time becoming united, assembled, and at rest, but also becoming seasick, dizzy, and vomiting (that is, confessing their offenses as though they were disease-producing bile—by which I mean the sins arising from bitterness and the evils heaped up from disorderly desires. By confessing these, as though you had vomited them, you are relieved of the illness and receive the saving health that comes from attentive care).","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"εὐσταθείτωσαν οὖν οἱ ἐπιβάται ἑδραῖοι ἐπὶ τῶν ἰδίων καθεζόμενοι τόπων","chosen":"The passengers, then, should keep steady, seated firmly in their own places","rationale":"Preserves both the call for steadiness and the image of passengers remaining firmly in their assigned places."},{"source_quote":"σεισμὸν ἢ ἑτεροκλινίαν","chosen":"rocking or a list to one side","rationale":"Distinguishes general shaking or rocking from the vessel’s unequal inclination toward one side."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ναυστολόγοι τοὺς μισθοὺς ὑπομιμνησκέτωσαν","chosen":"The ship’s recruiters should give reminders of the rewards","rationale":"Retains the shipboard role and renders μισθούς as rewards while avoiding an explicit recipient not stated in the clause."},{"source_quote":"καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς -ὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ","chosen":"should carefully prepare what is needed for each person","rationale":"This English is provisional and follows the conjecture τὰ χρῄζοντα; the supplied printed sequence -ὰ remains unresolved and is separately recorded as blocking publication."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ κυβερνήτου μόνου τοὺς λόγους ἀντιβαλλέτω","chosen":"should relay the words of the helmsman alone","rationale":"Places the exclusivity with κυβερνήτου, identifying the helmsman alone as the source of the words."},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς ὡς σωτὴρ κυβερνήτης","chosen":"The Messiah, as Savior and helmsman","rationale":"Renders independently titular χριστός as “Messiah” and preserves both σωτήρ and κυβερνήτης without collapsing the saving and nautical images."},{"source_quote":"ναυτιῶντες, ἰλιγγιῶντες, ἀπερῶντες","chosen":"becoming seasick, dizzy, and vomiting","rationale":"Follows the escalating bodily imagery and the author’s immediate explanation of the last term as expelling harmful bile through confession."},{"source_quote":"προσιέμενοι τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἐπιμελείας σωτήριον ὑγείαν","chosen":"receive the saving health that comes from attentive care","rationale":"Preserves the medical image of accepting health produced through care or treatment."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καταρτιζέτωσαν ἐπιμελῶς -ὰ χρῄζοντα ἑκάστῳ","issue":"The image-checked print supplies -ὰ before χρῄζοντα. Its function is unresolved: it may represent editorial notation, a damaged or defective printed sequence, or another typographic convention not established here. The English provisionally follows τὰ χρῄζοντα, but that reconstruction is a conjecture rather than the supplied reading, so coverage and lexical fidelity at this locus cannot yet be certified.","proposed_reading":"τὰ χρῄζοντα","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ ’ναῦται","issue":"The mark printed before ναῦται is not explained by ordinary elision, but that does not establish that it is accidental. Its possible editorial or typographic function remains unclear; the translation provisionally treats it as nonlexical without altering the supplied transcription.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρωρεὺς ’ἐγρηγορὼς","issue":"The mark printed before ἐγρηγορὼς is not required for the syntax and is not explained by ordinary elision, but it may still be an intentional editorial or typographic feature. The translation provisionally treats it as nonlexical without presenting an unmarked Greek form as an established correction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἀπερῶντες","issue":"The uncommon form is interpreted as vomiting or purging because the author immediately explains it through the expulsion of disease-producing bile and later uses ἀπεράσαντες in the same comparison. The general purgative sense is contextually strong, but the exact lexical formation remains uncertain.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
